The invention relates to a piezoelectric transformer having a piezoelectric element (1) of the length L, wherein an input voltage Uin can be applied on an input side (2) for being transformed into an output voltage Uout on the output side (3) according to a transformation ratio Uout/Uin=Ku. The piezoelectric element (1) comprises multiple plies (4a, 4b, 4c) of inner electrodes, which are arranged in multiple different layers (S1, S2, S3). Each ply (4a, 4b, 4c) of inner electrodes extends along at least one predetermined sub-section of a predetermined length, wherein sub-sections of plies (4a, 4c) of a first group of layers (S1, S3) and sub-sections of plies (4b) of a second group of layers (S2) have different dimensions, so that the piezoelectric transformer satisfies the following condition: Cin≤N2Cout, wherein Cin indicates the input capacitance, Cout indicates the output capacitance, and N indicates the transformation ratio of the ideal transformer.

outputs.L1: The invention relates to a piezoelectric transformer comprising a piezoelectric element (1) having a length L. An input voltage Uin can be applied to an input side (2) and transformed into an output voltage Uout at an output side (3) according to a transformation ratio Uout/Uin = Ku. The piezoelectric element (1) comprises multiple plies (4a, 4b, 4c) of inner electrodes arranged in multiple distinct layers (S1, S2, S3). Each ply (4a, 4b, 4c) of inner electrodes extends along at least one predetermined subsection having a predetermined length. The subsections of the plies (4a, 4c) in a first group of layers (S1, S3) and those of the plies (4b) in a second group of layers (S2) have different dimensions, such that the piezoelectric transformer satisfies the following condition: Cin ≤ N²Cout, wherein Cin denotes the input capacitance, Cout denotes the output capacitance, and N denotes the transformation ratio of the ideal transformer.
outputs.L2: The invention concerns a piezoelectric transformer that includes a piezoelectric element (1) with a length L. An input voltage Uin is supplied to an input side (2) and converted into an output voltage Uout at an output side (3), with the voltage conversion ratio defined as Uout/Uin = Ku. The piezoelectric element (1) contains several sets (4a, 4b, 4c) of internal electrodes positioned in different layers (S1, S2, S3). Each set of internal electrodes extends across at least one specified section having a predetermined length. The sections associated with electrode sets (4a, 4c) in a first layer group (S1, S3) differ in size from those associated with electrode sets (4b) in a second layer group (S2). These dimensional differences ensure that the transformer meets the condition Cin ≤ N²Cout, where Cin is the input capacitance, Cout is the output capacitance, and N is the transformation ratio of an ideal transformer.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a piezoelectric transformer comprising a piezoelectric element having an overall length \(L\). An input voltage \(U_{\text{in}}\) is applied to an input side of the transformer and converted into an output voltage \(U_{\text{out}}\). The voltage transformation ratio is defined as:

\[
\frac{U_{\text{out}}}{U_{\text{in}}}=K_u.
\]

The piezoelectric element includes multiple plies of inner electrodes arranged in different layers. Each electrode ply extends along at least one predetermined subsection of the piezoelectric element, with each subsection having a specified length.

The electrode plies are divided into at least a first layer group and a second layer group. The electrode subsections associated with these groups have different dimensions. These dimensions are selected so that the input capacitance \(C_{\text{in}}\) and the output capacitance \(C_{\text{out}}\) satisfy the following condition:

\[
C_{\text{in}} \leq N^2 C_{\text{out}},
\]

where \(N\) represents the relevant transformation parameter. This configuration allows the electrical properties of the input and output sides to be coordinated through the geometry and arrangement of the inner electrode plies.
outputs.L4:
A piezoelectric transformer includes a multilayer piezoelectric element having a plurality of piezoelectric layers and inner-electrode plies arranged in the stacking direction. At least some of the inner-electrode plies are divided into subsections having different dimensions. By selectively connecting these subsections to input and output terminals, the effective electrode areas—and therefore the capacitances—of the input and output portions can be adjusted independently.

When an alternating input voltage is applied to the input electrodes, the inverse piezoelectric effect causes the multilayer element to vibrate in a predetermined resonant mode. The resulting mechanical vibration is transmitted through the element to the output portion, where it is converted by the direct piezoelectric effect into an output voltage. The voltage transformation ratio is determined by the piezoelectric properties, the resonant mode, the number and arrangement of active layers, and the dimensions and electrical connections of the electrode subsections.

The differing subsection dimensions allow the input capacitance \(C_{\mathrm{in}}\) to be selected so that

\[
C_{\mathrm{in}} \leq N^{2} C_{\mathrm{out}},
\]

where \(C_{\mathrm{out}}\) is the output capacitance and \(N\) is the intended voltage-transformation ratio. Satisfying this relationship reduces the adverse effect of capacitive loading and brings the practical voltage ratio closer to that of an ideal transformer. The arrangement can therefore provide improved transformation efficiency and more predictable voltage conversion without requiring a substantial increase in the overall size of the piezoelectric element.
outputs.L5: The relationship between **Uin** and **Uout** describes how an electronic circuit processes a voltage signal. **Uin** represents the input voltage applied to the circuit, while **Uout** is the resulting output voltage. Depending on the circuit design, Uout may be higher, lower, inverted, or otherwise modified compared with Uin. The ratio \(Uout/Uin\) is often used to determine the circuit’s voltage gain.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an invention concerning a multilayer piezoelectric transformer whose electrode dimensions are configured to satisfy Cin≤N²Cout.
counterfactuals.output: A multilayer piezoelectric transformer includes a piezoelectric body having a plurality of laminated piezoelectric layers, at least one input electrode section, and at least one output electrode section. Dimensions, overlap areas, spacing, and/or numbers of the input and output electrodes are selected such that an input capacitance \(C_{\mathrm{in}}\) and an output capacitance \(C_{\mathrm{out}}\) satisfy \(C_{\mathrm{in}} \leq N^{2}C_{\mathrm{out}}\), where \(N\) is a voltage transformation ratio of the transformer. The capacitance relationship may be established by independently configuring electrode lengths, widths, layer counts, or dielectric thicknesses in the input and output sections. Satisfaction of the relationship reduces capacitive loading and suppresses degradation of voltage conversion efficiency, thereby enabling improved power transfer, reduced losses, and stable operation over a desired load range while maintaining a compact multilayer structure.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an improved multilayer piezoelectric transformer in patent language, explaining how the dimensions of electrode sub-sections in first and second layer groups ensure a specified relationship between input capacitance, output capacitance, and the ideal transformation ratio.
counterfactuals.output:
An improved multilayer piezoelectric transformer comprises a piezoelectric body having a first layer group defining an input portion and a second layer group defining an output portion. Each layer group includes a plurality of piezoelectric layers and internal electrodes. At least selected internal electrodes are divided into electrically interconnected electrode sub-sections, the length, width, overlap area, spacing, and number of the sub-sections being independently selectable in the first and second layer groups.

The effective input and output capacitances are determined substantially by the summed active overlap areas of the respective electrode sub-sections, according to:

\[
C_{\mathrm{in}}\approx
\sum_i \frac{\varepsilon_i A_{1i}}{d_{1i}},
\qquad
C_{\mathrm{out}}\approx
\sum_j \frac{\varepsilon_j A_{2j}}{d_{2j}},
\]

where \(A_{1i}\) and \(A_{2j}\) are the effective overlap areas of the sub-sections in the first and second layer groups, respectively, and \(d_{1i}\) and \(d_{2j}\) are the corresponding piezoelectric-layer thicknesses.

The dimensions and number of the electrode sub-sections are selected so that, for a specified ideal voltage transformation ratio \(N_{\mathrm{id}}=V_{\mathrm{out}}/V_{\mathrm{in}}\),

\[
\frac{C_{\mathrm{in}}}{C_{\mathrm{out}}}
=
N_{\mathrm{id}}^{\,2},
\]

or, equivalently,

\[
N_{\mathrm{id}}=
\sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{in}}}{C_{\mathrm{out}}}}.
\]

Thus, for substantially equal dielectric constants and layer thicknesses, the aggregate active electrode areas satisfy:

\[
\frac{\sum_i A_{1i}}{\sum_j A_{2j}}
=
N_{\mathrm{id}}^{\,2}.
\]

Where the layer thicknesses or dielectric constants differ, the electrode dimensions are instead selected to satisfy:

\[
\frac{
\sum_i \varepsilon_i A_{1i}/d_{1i}
}{
\sum_j \varepsilon_j A_{2j}/d_{2j}
}
=
N_{\mathrm{id}}^{\,2}.
\]

Accordingly, the desired capacitance relationship may be obtained without changing the external dimensions or principal mechanical-resonance dimensions of the transformer. Adjustment may be effected by changing the width or length of one or more electrode sub-sections, omitting selected sub-sections, or changing the number of electrically parallel sub-sections in either layer group. The mechanical coupling region can therefore remain substantially unchanged while the electrical capacitance ratio is matched to the ideal transformation ratio, thereby reducing reactive mismatch and improving voltage-transfer efficiency.

If the transformation ratio is defined inversely as \(V_{\mathrm{in}}/V_{\mathrm{out}}\), the corresponding capacitance relationship is likewise inverted.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
